problem: The coverage report is applied to scores even when coverage is disabled or filtered (not measured). A baseline taken then carries the penalty but not coverage in `sources`; enabling coverage later zeroes a penalty the baseline already paid and the fold subtracts it again.
impact: Drift in already-measured sources is hidden up to the coverage penalty: a 10-point eslint regression read as 'improved' (regression -5); 20 points read only WARN.
suggested_fix: Make 'scored' and 'measured' agree for coverage: count coverage as measured whenever its data was applied, or never apply unmeasured coverage data.
evidence: probe3.test.ts N2 vs control N2c on d74b535c.

problem: The fold's per-scope behaviour is asserted only on the project scope; folding only `project`, or adding scopes not in the baseline, leaves the suite green.
impact: A regression to project-only folding leaves every module holding the new source's findings with a permanent false regression while CI stays green.
suggested_fix: Steady-state test over a module: fold, run again unchanged, assert every scope regression 0 and not 'regressed'; assert no scope is added by the fold.
evidence: Mutant Q02b: bun test src/health 180 pass; a steady-state probe then shows module:src/alpha regression 30.

problem: The fold uses clamped scores, so a scope clamped at 0 records a new source's effect as 0.
impact: Fails loud: the new source's pre-existing findings later read as a regression (N1b: FAIL regression 30).
suggested_fix: Compute the effect from unclamped penalties and fold as clamp(base - effect).
quote: const folded = Math.min(100, Math.max(0, metric.health_score + metric.regression_score));

problem: A module/file re-baseline writes a score measured with a source the recorded set lacks; the next whole-project fold subtracts that source's effect a second time.
impact: That scope reads improved by the effect, hiding a regression up to it.
suggested_fix: Refuse a module/file re-baseline while the report measured an unrecorded source.
evidence: service.ts keeps the file's set for module/file; the fold runs only on project runs.
quote: const rewritesAll = input.scope === undefined || input.scope.kind === "project" || input.scope.kind === "changed";

problem: The module re-baseline assertion is vacuous: the recorded and measured sets are equal at that point.
impact: Deleting the module/file branch of rewritesAll stays green.
suggested_fix: Make the measured set differ from the recorded one before the module update.
